answer: The Registered domain bound by challenge-response signature with annual re-verification makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the challenge-response signature is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Like a ember on a key ring, one odd key hides easily, so the check runs on every binding rather than a sample. Between a tide and a comet lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to bind.
